newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Jan value of production down 6.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Jan value of production down 6.3 pct.

text.p: The Philippine value of production index in January fell by 6.3 percent year-on-year, the National Statistics Office reported on Friday.

The value of production index of key manufacturing enterprises slipped to 406.9 in January 1997 from 434.4 in the year-ago month, as double-digit decreases were posted in six major sectors, the agency said.

These were felt in miscellaneous manufacturers with a decline of 25.4 percent; textile, 22.9 percent; basic metals, 21.1 percent; transport equipment, 18.6 percent; paper and paper products, 14.8 percent; and petroleum products, 14.4 percent.
Similarly, the volume of production index also shrank by 9.1 percent to 135.9 in January 1997 from 149.5. This measures change in volume, net of inflation.

Double-digit declines were observed in eight sectors. These are paper and paper products, 28.7 percent; wearing apparel, 27.1 percent; petroleum products, 26.3 percent; other manufacturing industries, 19.5 percent; textile, 18.5 percent; iron and steel, 17.1 percent; transport equipment, 16.0 percent; and glass and glass products, 13.6 percent.
However, on a month-on-month basis, the value of production index increased by 2.9 percent and volume of production rose by 2.5 percent, the agency said.

These indexes are intended to give flash indicators on the performance of key manufacturing activities and are based on a sample of 422 manufacturing establishments mostly located in Metro Manila with a response rate of 81 percent, the agency said.
